title: Why I think achievements boost sales.
author: Derreus
selftext:
I’ve been making my own game and have been lurking in a lot of the game dev subs. One thing I have not seen mentioned once is to have achievements in your game.

I know I might be part of a minority, but I’m an achievement hunter at heart. I have games that have sat in my steam wishlist for years hoping that at some point they’ll add achievements.

Often times they don’t even need to be groundbreaking as long as they are actually achievable (no multiplayer locked, RNG based, or mega scale “get 1 million of a thing” achievements). There are entire communities that revolve around buying games with the sole intent of adding another 100% game to their list.

I wanted to see what others on here think about this. Are achievements a deciding factor for some of you?

comments.author: Derreus
comments.body:
The game I’m making is a foraging tycoon game where players scale up their operations progressively.

Some achievements I’m thinking of adding are:

\- Property related achievements (new growing facility, a patch of growing land, market booths)  
\- vehicle related achievements (larger vehicles mean more inventory for transporting hauls)  
\- employee achievements (number of employees, different types of employees)

I’m sure I’ll think of more as I continue, but it’s never too  late to start picturing how you could create engaging achievements for your game.

comments.author: waaachow
comments.body: Yes, good trophies motivate me to get so much more out of a game I’m enjoying. I’ve got a prototype space tactics game on itch and I’ve added in game achievements for now.

replies.author: Derreus
replies.body: That’s definitely a good call! Let me know if you notice any difference in play time.

comments.author: Am_Biyori
comments.body: The topic does come up occasionally, and I'm surprized at how important they are to a lot of people. Wasn't going to bother with them but gotta change course I guess.

replies.author: Derreus
replies.body: Other than maybe all of the clip art you need, they seem quite basic to setup. I think it’s that extra 1% that could net you some unexpected sales!

comments.author: EC36339
comments.body: I think it says a lot (and nothing good) if you have to gamify gaming.
